_doc:
Full audiobook blueprint run: ingest → plan → cast → narrate → stitch. The FIRST live exercise of multi-voice voice-acting: it calls the `audiobook-casting` WM worker (pinning its output shape with the correct schema), real kokoro TTS on mini2, and the video_compiler concat. The harness has no file-upload step, so the manuscript rides inline in `manuscript_fixture`; the validator stages it via POST /api/uploads/manuscript and injects the ref into brief.manuscript_ref before creating the project. `chapter_mode:single` + a ~6-line two-speaker excerpt keeps narrate to a handful of TTS calls. `voice_acting:true` enables LLM casting; `voice_cast` pins one character so the override path runs. pause_after_stages:[] overrides the blueprint's ingest+cast pauses so the run goes straight to `completed`. `expect_stage_assertions` proves the cast produced >=2 distinct voices and stitch produced an artifact — green alone would not prove voices are distinct.

FLOOR PINNED, NOT RE-SIZED (recorded 2026-09-03). `audiobook_cast casting[].voice_id >= 2` was flagged fragile because MEASURED over a 90-day window of completed `stage_outputs` the distinct voice count is min = max = 2 (n=3) -- floor exactly ON the observed minimum, on a sample far too thin to size a number from. Pinning is the honest answer: the cast is AUTHORED, not chosen -- `project.voice.voice_id` names the narrator (af_heart) and `brief.voice_cast` names exactly one character voice (Alice -> bf_emma), so 1 + 1 = 2 distinct voices is what the input pins and what all 3 runs returned. Lowering to 1 would make the check pass on a run that cast the narrator for EVERYTHING, i.e. on the exact multi-voice regression this scenario is the first live exercise of. tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py now derives the pin as 1 + len(brief.voice_cast) and requires this floor to EQUAL it, so adding a character to the cast without raising the floor reds in CI.

manuscript_fixture.text:
The afternoon was warm, and Alice sat by the riverbank with nothing to do.
"I wonder what time it is," Alice said, peering down the long grassy slope.
A white rabbit hurried past, muttering to himself as he checked a small pocket watch.
Alice rose to her feet at once. "How curious! A rabbit with a waistcoat and a watch."
She followed him across the meadow, determined not to lose sight of so strange a creature.
Down the rabbit went, into a hole beneath the hedge, and down went Alice after him.

_pixel_doc:
Media ACCEPTANCE probes on the delivered master (scripts/e2e_validate.py _MEDIA_CHECKS). Before these, this scenario proved a url was a non-blank string and nothing about the bytes behind it. `artifact_reachable` proves the object downloads and decodes; `audio_present` proves an audio stream exists AND is not digital silence (ffmpeg volumedetect mean/peak dBFS); `resolution` reads the ENCODED width/height, not the number the stage reports about itself; `stream_durations` measures the VIDEO and AUDIO stream durations SEPARATELY and never the container -- a container duration is the MAX over its streams, so it can never refute a truncated video track. Floors are the ones this scenario's existing green assertions already prove, never new tuning numbers.

`duration_within_tolerance` is present but DISARMED (`"enabled": false`). It compares the delivered stream length against `ordered_seconds` at the SAME +/-10% the pipeline's own duration_conformance uses. Flip `enabled` to true to arm it -- deliberately not armed while the duration calibration work is in flight, because a red instrument on known-in-flight work teaches people to ignore the instrument.

expect_pixel_checks._doc: Header-vs-decoded guard on the delivered audiobook. This was deliberately OMITTED at first because audio could not be measured: ffprobe publishes no avg_frame_rate (and no frame_size) for an audio stream, so the packet-count route that measures video returns nothing and the probe fell back to the header -- i.e. an assertion that could not fail, which is worse than none. Audio is now measured by DECODING (ffmpeg -f null - with -progress, reading out_time_us), so the exclusion no longer applies and is removed. It matters most HERE: audiobook is the one type whose entire deliverable IS the audio, with no video track to cross-check against, so before this it was the last place a truncated master could read completely clean. THE incident this guards: a moov declaring 12.0s over content that decodes to 2.81s -- every header-reading duration assertion believes the 12.0.
